title: Construct a reversible finite below-floor zero for the 679-owner control
body:
A scoped rank-two chart difference across 127 root coordinates prepares and retires 254 zeros while restoring dirty escrow and the retained complement. The separate scalar lift restores all histories with explicit backing.

## Scope and source

Starts from the #7912/#7929 owner namespace. The 451-factor result binds logical addressing; a full chart-aware graded MOVE or finite supplier remains open. The 36-call signed change is zero. The source comparator is #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`. The included source manifest identifies every public dependency used.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-bit679-reversible-zero/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory, check its checksum manifest, and run the extracted commands. `python3 -I -B verify.py` passed from a clean copy, including dirty, short-stock, alias and omitted-ADD controls. Hosted execution is separate.

## Open next questions

Bind the cell to physical stock and all factor addresses before applying the complete 451 supplier.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. [Campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
